assessment: B-level decision page for "https vs http" (1600/mo, KD 33): the verdict card answers the choice above the fold, every H2 opens with a direct answer, and the recommendation is backed by AEOeye's own measurements (AEOeye Technical SEO Baseline (391 sites, 2026-10-24)) with limitations stated.

topic.readerProblem: A site owner deciding "https vs http" needs a straight recommendation and the evidence for it.
topic.connection: The free SEO audit flags exactly this decision on real sites (redirect types, HTTPS, structure, image formats); the page links into it.

sources.supports: HTTPS is a very lightweight ranking signal, affecting fewer than 1% of queries (2014).
Redirects are a strong canonical signal; Google prefers HTTPS over HTTP as canonical.
From July 2018 (Chrome 68) Chrome marks all HTTP sites "not secure".
HSTS syntax: max-age, includeSubDomains, preload; ignored over plain HTTP.

checks: Re-read every factual claim against the cited primary sources, fetched on 2026-10-24 (7 sources listed on the page); unverifiable statements were removed or reworded before publishing.
content-lint passed with no errors: 1245 words, 2 Pexels images, 10 inline source links, 4 internal links, 4 FAQs, 10 H2 sections.
Title/H1, secondary-keyword H2s and meta description match the locked three-round plan in docs/seo-v2/final-table.json.
Rendered on the local build at a 375 px mobile viewport: no horizontal overflow (document scrollWidth equals the viewport width).
Recomputed every figure quoted from AEOeye Technical SEO Baseline (391 sites, 2026-10-24) from the raw files in /public/resources.

artifacts.description: AEOeye Technical SEO Baseline (391 sites, 2026-10-24) — the raw data behind the figures quoted in this decision page.

methodology: Figures come from AEOeye's own zero-cost measurements published under /resources: plain HTTP requests from a self-identified research user agent (AEOeyeResearch), robots.txt respected, 1 s between requests per domain; encoding tests run locally with cwebp/avifenc and SSIM via ffmpeg. Each dataset file states its exact method.
limitations: Convenience sample of well-known sites (not the whole web), homepages only, a single snapshot on 2026-10-24; the image test covers 20 screenshots, not photographs.
